cards.explanation: The cry is asking whether the LORD is still in Zion. It says, “Is the LORD no longer in Zion? Is her King no longer there?” (Jeremiah 8:19). I think it sounds like someone calling from far away who can't see Him anywhere. That's a lonely question, friends.

The answer is idols. The LORD asks, “Why have they provoked Me to anger with their carved images, with their worthless foreign idols?” (Jeremiah 8:19). He names them twice in one breath, carved images and foreign idols. That's what the question points at.

The answer is False. The verse says, “The harvest has passed, the summer has ended, but we have not been saved.” (Jeremiah 8:20). Time keeps moving and the saving hasn't arrived. It sounds like people who've waited out a whole season for help and are still waiting.

The real question underneath is why the people still aren't healed. The speaker asks, “Is there no balm in Gilead? Is no physician there?” and then asks, “Why then has the health of the daughter of my people not been restored?” (Jeremiah 8:22). The medicine and the doctor are right there in the question. The real ache is that the healing hasn't come.

He wishes for a traveler's lodge so he could leave his people. He says, “If only I had a traveler’s lodge in the wilderness, I would abandon my people and depart from them…” (Jeremiah 9:2). That's a big turn after all those tears, friends. I think he's worn all the way down.

The reason the verse gives is that they are all faithless. He says, “…for they are all adulterers, a crowd of faithless people.” (Jeremiah 9:2). That's a hard thing to say about your own people. It comes right after tears, so I think this man loves them and is still worn out by what he sees.

The LORD tells everyone to guard against his neighbor. He says, “Let everyone guard against his neighbor…” (Jeremiah 9:4). Lies prevail over truth in the land, and that's why He gives the warning. It's a sad picture, friends, when even a neighbor is someone to guard against.

The answer is False. The LORD says, “do not trust any brother, for every brother deals craftily, and every friend spreads slander.” (Jeremiah 9:4). The warning covers the neighbor, the brother and the friend. It's a land where trust has worn very thin.

The deceivers refuse to know the LORD. He says, “You dwell in the midst of deception; in their deceit they refuse to know Me…” (Jeremiah 9:6). The word is refuse, friends. Deception is all around, and the deceivers won't know Him.

The LORD of Hosts says He will refine them and test them. He says, “Behold, I will refine them and test them, for what else can I do because of the daughter of My people?” (Jeremiah 9:7). Notice the question tucked inside, “…what else can I do…” I think that sounds like someone with a heavy heart.

In his heart, that man is setting a trap for his neighbor. The verse says, “With his mouth a man speaks peace to his neighbor, but in his heart he sets a trap for him.” (Jeremiah 9:8). Peace is on the lips, and a trap is in the heart. That gap between mouth and heart is the deception the LORD keeps pointing at.

The answer is False. The LORD asks, “Should I not punish them for these things?” and then, “Should I not avenge Myself on such a nation as this?” (Jeremiah 9:9). He doesn't say He'll let it slide. It's a heavy moment, and the passage doesn't hurry past it.

The weeping is because the land has been scorched and left empty. The mountains and pasture “…have been scorched so no one passes through, and the lowing of cattle is not heard.” (Jeremiah 9:10). So the weeping comes from the scorched, empty land. It's a quiet picture, friends, and a sad one.
The answer is True. The verse says, “Both the birds of the air and the beasts have fled; they have gone away.” (Jeremiah 9:10). No cattle lowing, no birds, no beasts. That's an empty land.
